paragraphs.title: They did not dispossess the Canaanites

The children of Manasseh
The priests

easy.question: What happened to the Canaanite according to verse 12?
answers: The Canaanite was allowed to dwell in that land
The Canaanite was completely expelled
The Canaanite was killed in battle
easy.explanation: The verse says the Canaanite would dwell in that land — they remained living there.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do to the Canaanites when they became strong according to verse 13?
answers: They gave them freedom as free citizens
They drove them out of all the land
They put the Canaanites to tribute
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says the Israelites put the Canaanites to tribute — they subjected them to forced labor or payment rather than driving them out.

medium.question: What is the main difference between the description in verse 12 and verse 13?
answers: Verse 12 says Manasseh failed to drive out the Canaanites; verse 13 says later, when Israel became strong, they put the Canaanites to tribute but did not drive them out
Both verses describe the same single event where Manasseh expelled the Canaanites entirely
These verses actually refer to the tribe of Ephraim, not Manasseh
medium.explanation: Verse 12 records Manasseh's inability to expel them; verse 13 shows a later, broader Israelite response of subjugation (tribute) without complete expulsion.

medium.question: What does 'put the Canaanites to tribute' mean in verse 13? (context: "put the Canaanites to tribute")
answers: To expel them from the land
To make them servants or subject them to forced labor/tribute
To grant them land as full citizens
medium.explanation: The phrase means the Canaanites were made to pay tribute or serve under Israelite control — they were not expelled.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'did not utterly drive them out' imply about what Israel did?
answers: They expelled the Canaanites from the entire area
They made the Canaanites servants instead of expelling them
They granted the Canaanites full equality and land rights
medium.explanation: It indicates they did not remove the people; instead, they subjected them to tribute or servitude while they remained in the land.

challenge.question: Why does verse 12 refer to 'the children of Manasseh' but verse 13 mentions 'the children of Israel'?
answers: The verses contradict each other and make it unclear who acted
It indicates Manasseh was singled out for a reprimand
The first verse describes a local failure by Manasseh to expel inhabitants; the second describes a later time when Israel as a whole subdued the Canaanites differently
challenge.explanation: The shift in subject implies a change in scale or time: initially Manasseh couldn't expel them; later, when Israel overall became strong, they imposed tribute instead.

challenge.question: What historical or geographic conclusion can be drawn from these verses about the conquest of the land?
answers: That the conquest was not total and Canaanite populations remained living under Israelite control in some areas
That the land was completely taken and no Canaanites remained
That all Canaanites were immediately given full citizenship among Israel
challenge.explanation: The verses show incomplete conquest — some Canaanites remained in place and were subjected to tribute, indicating partial control rather than total expulsion.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'did not utterly drive them out' emphasize in its repetition? (context: "did not utterly drive them out")
answers: That a formal legal transfer of land to the Canaanites took place
The repetition stresses that they did not expel the inhabitants even when they were strong
That Israel renounced its land claims and handed it to the Canaanites
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording highlights that despite Israel's strength, they did not completely remove the inhabitants; the repetition emphasizes the failure to expel them.

paragraphs.title: The request of Joseph's descendants and Joshua's reply

The children of Joseph
The tribe of Judah

answers: They were given only one lot and one portion to inherit though they are numerous
They had no water in their land
Joshua asked them to fight alone
easy.explanation: They argued that they had received only one lot despite being a great people and expected more land.

easy.question: What military problem did they mention regarding the people of the valley?
answers: They speak a different language
They use advanced bows
They have chariots of iron
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says the Canaanites in the valley have chariots of iron — a military advantage that makes conquest difficult.

medium.question: What did Joshua tell the children of Joseph to do if they were a great people?
answers: Remain in the valley and wait for help
Join other tribes and fight together
Go up to the wooded hill country and clear out the land of the Perizzites and the giants
medium.explanation: Joshua replied they should go up to the forested mountain region and clear it out — the Perizzites and Rephaim — if Mount Ephraim was too narrow.

medium.question: What does 'the outgoings of it shall be thine' mean in this context?
answers: The produce or yield of the land
The people who live there

medium.explanation: 'Outgoings' refers to the produce or yield — Joshua promises the mountain and its produce will be theirs.

medium.explanation: Verse 16 specifically names Beth‑shean and the valley of Jezreel as places whose inhabitants have iron chariots.

challenge.explanation: Joshua tells them they are a great people and will not be limited to one lot; the mountain will be theirs after clearing it.

Because the valley's inhabitants were strong and had chariots of iron, making them hard to expel
Because Joshua banned cities in the valley for religious reasons
challenge.explanation: The passage notes the valley inhabitants had iron chariots and were strong, explaining why the valley wasn't easily given to Joseph's descendants.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'for they have chariots of iron, and they are strong' mean in the military context of the verse?
answers: They have a strong alliance with their neighbors
They preserve a longstanding tradition
The Canaanites are militarily powerful with iron chariots, making them difficult to displace

verses_kJV: There was also a lot for the tribe of Manasseh; for he was the firstborn of Joseph; to wit, for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead: because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families; for the children of Abiezer, and for the children of Helek, and for the children of Asriel, and for the children of Shechem, and for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph by their families.

But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren. Therefore according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.
And there fell ten portions to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan, which were on the other side Jordan;
Because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons: and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.
And the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah, that lieth before Shechem; and the border went along on the right hand unto the inhabitants of Entappuah.
Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim;

And the coast descended unto the river Kanah, southward of the river: these cities of Ephraim are among the cities of Manasseh: the coast of Manasseh also was on the north side of the river, and the outgoings of it were at the sea:
Southward it was Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, and the sea is his border; and they met together in Asher on the north, and in Issachar on the east.

And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Bethshean and her towns, and Ibleam and her towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Endor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Taanach and her towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and her towns, even three countries.
Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.
Yet it came to pass, when the children of Israel were waxen strong, that they put the Canaanites to tribute, but did not utterly drive them out.
And the children of Joseph spake unto Joshua, saying, Why hast thou given me but one lot and one portion to inherit, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as the Lord hath blessed me hitherto?

And Joshua answered them, If thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, and cut down for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee.

And the children of Joseph said, The hill is not enough for us: and all the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they who are of Bethshean and her towns, and they who are of the valley of Jezreel.
And Joshua spake unto the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, Thou art a great people, and hast great power: thou shalt not have one lot only:

But the mountain shall be thine; for it is a wood, and thou shalt cut it down: and the outgoings of it shall be thine: for thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots, and though they be strong.
